title: JANUS Engine — dedicated research-branch manifest

latest_findings.magnetic_baseline: Coreless/slotless axial-flux PM starter-generator remains the preferred first Axle drive because it provides low-cogging battery spinup, RPM control and regeneration in one bidirectional machine.
latest_findings.micro_EPM_refinement: TOPA/Spider found that small electropermanent magnets can switch with milli-joule pulses and zero holding power, so per-sector gated magnetic assist is not categorically rejected. It is reopened as an A/B branch provided real torque across the JANUS gap is sufficient and total switching watts remain below the energy saved.
latest_findings.micro_EPM_screen: At 8 switching events per revolution, 5.8-10 mJ/event corresponds to about 0.23-0.40 W at 300 RPM and 0.46-0.80 W at 600 RPM. At 16 events/rev the same range is about 0.46-0.80 W at 300 RPM and 0.93-1.60 W at 600 RPM. These are switching-only figures; force, drivers, hysteresis, eddy-current and reliability losses remain unmeasured.
latest_findings.battery_startup: External precharge -> battery spinup/auxiliary support -> gill/PEMFC state convergence -> load transfer -> first surplus restores reserve SOC -> export only above reserve recovery.
latest_findings.self_drive_rule: External charger disconnected and SOC_end >= SOC_start over the stabilized hold after all pumps, fans, magnetic electronics and controls are charged.

next_actions: Bench coreless AFPM and micro-EPM assist against the same Axle load profile.
Measure total Wh from S0_OFF to target RPM and through the startup hold, not just peak torque.
For EPM branch measure E_switch, field on/off ratio, assist torque, residual braking torque, thermal rise and switch lifetime.
Select micro-EPM assist only if it reduces integrated battery Wh more than all switching and driver losses; otherwise keep AFPM-only baseline.
